BERLIN, Oct 16 : Bayern Munich are edging closer to their very best despite drawing their last two matches, coach Vincent Kompany said on Friday. The German champions, who take on visitors RB Leipzig on Saturday, have drawn their last two matches in all competitions – a 2-2 against Augsburg that included conceding the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, followed by a 3-3 at rank outsiders Viking in the Champions League on Tuesday. They looked far from convincing in both matches, missing chances and looking shaky at the back, and having to come from behind both times to rescue draws. They are currently in third spot in the Bundesliga, two points behind leaders Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund.

"We want to attack," Kompany told a press conference. "We have the feeling that there are a lot of things behind the perception of these two results. I have the feeling it is just before we show our very best version. "In the last two matches we shot 50 times on goal. If we do a few things better then we are not too far from our very best version." Bayern have busy weeks coming up and after Leipzig – they face Arsenal in the Champions League before taking on leaders Freiburg in the Bundesliga. They then host Dortmund in Der Klassiker on October 31 after a German Cup second-round match against Magdeburg. "These moments that some people think might be difficult we say these are the best moments you can have in your career. If you win these matches then you have created some moments," Kompany said. "We are sharp and motivated... we look forward to these matches to measure ourselves against the best. "The lads reach the limit in every training session and it is fun to watch. They know it is now best to talk on the pitch."

Source: Reuters

FAST

SAN FRANCISCO: Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday (Oct 15) and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car. The white two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX, drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using built-in thrusters. Later in the event it used the thrusters to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the maneuver. Some watchers saw the collaboration as Musk drumming up interest in a merger of the two big companies he controls, an idea he has explored by discussing their overlap.

The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors. "It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on social media platform X. "The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said. Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially". But the car still carries symbolic weight.

"Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month. Viewers and witnesses gushed over the spectacle of the launch. "That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X. "I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI." Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of US$200,000 for the vehicle. Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed a "Performance" version of the vehicle requiring a US$50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a US$250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla says is "invite only", is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system". "HALFWAY TO THE SPEED OF SOUND" The event at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: Dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown. "This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX engineers working closely together to make something that you haven't seen in any movie," Musk, wearing a silver Western-style belt buckle emblazoned with the Tesla logo, told a cheering crowd of enthusiasts and investors. The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 97 kmh in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 370 kmh, Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy said.

Tesla unveils its long-delayed Roadster nearly a decade after first revealing a next-generation version of its original electric sports car, at a launch event in Waco, Texas, US, on Oct 15, 2026, in this still image taken from a handout video. (Image: Tesla/Handout via Reuters)

Tesla unveils its long-delayed Roadster nearly a decade after first revealing a next-generation version of its original electric sports car, at a launch event in Waco, Texas, US, on Oct 15, 2026, in this still image taken from a handout video. (Image: Tesla/Handout via Reuters)

"Definitely much faster than that," an excited Musk said. "I think you've got to crack halfway to the speed of sound." The Roadster can also travel over 480km on a single charge. That is less than half of what Musk promised in 2017, when Tesla first revealed a prototype of the second-generation Roadster and said that deliveries would begin in 2020. The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever electric vehicle and used a Lotus Elise chassis. It helped change the world's view of what an EV could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans. The reveal of the second-generation Roadster comes amid a sharp shift in Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers. This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab - a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors. Tesla is set to report third-quarter results on Oct 21. Sales of Tesla's aging lineup of EVs have declined over the past two years, although high gas prices helped boost deliveries in the third quarter. "The margin and cash flow numbers will carry far more weight with investors than anything they saw at the reveal," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for Asia-Pacific at trading platform eToro.

Source: Reuters/lk

Oct 16 : The US dollar was set for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, as investors turned their focus to the US rate outlook while concerns about an escalation of the Iran conflict faded. AI stocks have cratered this week and the stress has spread to parts of the credit market as investors who have crowded into bets all along the AI supply chain worry data centre operators might not manage to be profitable in time to pay their debts.  Analysts noted that Wednesday's market moves may provide a preview of how currencies would react to a major AI-driven selloff, with the dollar falling instead of attracting safe-haven demand as investors shift towards a more dovish view of the Federal Reserve policy path. The Swiss franc again looks set to be the biggest beneficiary, thanks to its safe-haven status and expectations that, even in a lower-rates environment, Switzerland is unlikely to cut policy rates below the current zero level. It was set for a 0.61 per cent weekly rise versus the dollar.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major peers, fell 0.25 per cent to 101.77 and was set for a 0.45 per cent weekly decline. It rose in two of the week's five sessions, including on Wednesday, as the boost from hotter-than-expected inflation data more than offset the drag from a selloff in tech stocks. The S&P 500 ended higher on Thursday, springing back from early losses as investors concerned about AI stocks shifted into healthcare and consumer stocks.  Wednesday’s “action revealed exactly what could threaten the US dollar and bring US yields lower in the next few months and in 2027: a reduction in the outlook for AI investment,” Thierry Wizman, global forex and rates strategist at Macquarie Group, said. “That's because it would reduce bond supply and impair US growth, all else equal,” he added. US RATES IN FOCUS US Treasury yields dropped earlier this week despite hot inflation readings as cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials tempered October hike expectations. Markets assign an 87 per cent probability to the Federal Reserve keeping rates unchanged later this month, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. Investors expect US President Donald Trump to steer clear of any escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a broader conflict could hurt his standing ahead of the midterm elections fuelling inflation and possibly hurting the economy. The euro was up 0.14 per cent to $1.1235 after climbing 0.56 per cent on Thursday in its biggest daily rise in two months. It was on track for a 0.39 per cent weekly gain. "Barring another big leg down in AI stocks and risk assets in general, expect the dollar to consolidate near recent highs," said Chris Turner, forex strategist at ING. "It is only when short-end rates break lower that the dollar is ready to drop. And we are not there yet," he added. The yen was on track for a 0.28 per cent weekly rise after dropping for four consecutive weeks as the Iran conflict supported the greenback. It was last up 0.05 per cent at 157.89. Higher oil prices tend to support the dollar while weighing on energy-importing currencies such as the euro and yen. The Japanese currency tumbled in mid-September after a disappointing Bank of Japan policy meeting, but subsequently fell by around 0.30 per cent a week as monetary tightening rhetoric by Japan's authorities supported the yen. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Friday that the BoJ would continue to raise policy rates in line with economic and financial developments.  The Australian dollar rose 0.55 per cent to $0.6959 but was an outlier in heading for a fall of 0.3 per cent on the dollar this week, after a surprisingly soft jobs report on Thursday had markets paring back expectations for another rise in interest rates.

Source: Reuters

FAST

TOKYO, Oct 16 : Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda on Friday reiterated the risks of underlying inflation overshooting the central bank's 2 per cent target, stressing the growing importance of keeping price pressures anchored around that level. In a speech read out by Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida at a meeting of Japanese credit unions, Ueda said factors including tensions in the Middle East, AI-related demand and currency swings could affect Japan's economy and prices, pointing to a risk that underlying inflation could exceed the BOJ's price target. "The perspective of anchoring underlying inflation at around 2 per cent has become more important than before," Ueda said, highlighting the need to ensure that any overshoot of the BOJ's target does not harm the economy. The speech, which largely repeated remarks Ueda made earlier this month, comes ahead of the BOJ's October 29 and 30 policy meeting, when the central bank will release fresh quarterly growth and inflation forecasts that market participants will scrutinise for clues on the timing of the next rate hike. The BOJ raised its key rate to a 31-year high last month, while signalling that it had entered a phase focused on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its target, raising the prospect of tighter policy.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Oct 16 : Toyota Motor expects its Arene software platform will be deployed in 10 million new vehicles annually and 50 car models by 2030, the company said on Friday, after the Nikkei reported the automaker aims to make those models software-defined by then. Chief Technology Officer Hiroki Nakajima outlined deployment plans for Arene at an investor briefing in Brussels last week, according to a Toyota spokesperson. Nakajima also said Toyota aims to expand the platform's deployment further as it moves towards 2035, including in vehicles from alliance partners, the spokesperson said. Toyota first introduced Arene in its revamped RAV4 sport utility vehicle, which was launched in 2025. Software-defined vehicles allow functions to be updated over the air after purchase, enabling automakers to add safety, autonomous driving and entertainment features without requiring customers to visit dealerships.

BENGALURU: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behaviour worldwide. AI model providers had voluntarily disclosed that their agents "exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks" during test runs to access Indian firms' data, including business records, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said late on Thursday (Oct 15). It did not name the providers or the affected organisations. The disclosure brings India into a growing global debate over how AI companies test models with advanced hacking abilities. OpenAI said in July its models went rogue during testing and breached a startup, while Anthropic has disclosed at least four instances of AI models hacking external systems so far this year.

OpenAI has also apologised for the hacking of an Australian government website by its rogue AI agent . None of the affected Indian entities detected the intrusions themselves, and in every case it was the AI companies that flagged the incidents, CERT-In said. In a second set of cases, the government agency's own investigations found attackers deliberately using freely available AI tools to probe Indian systems and break in for financial gain, with such tools deployed widely across infrastructure in multiple countries. Attacks that once took days from first entry to final damage were compressed to a few hours, CERT-In said, and victims that failed to fully clean up were attacked again within days, at greater depth.

NEW DELHI: Security was stepped up and police warned of traffic disruptions in the Indian capital Delhi on Friday (Oct 16) as the "cockroach" movement called for a rally in the central business district, its latest in a series of protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief. The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party, opposition groups, and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.

CJP and left-wing student groups have urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag. Delhi Police, however, urged people not to join "such assemblies", and the civic authority announced late on Thursday that the park itself would be closed for two days "due to administrative reasons".

Security personnel and police detain a journalist during a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in New Delhi, India, Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Adnan Abidi)

Police said they can facilitate a group of select people to carry the national flag and sing the national anthem at a "suitable place". Traders in the area petitioned the Supreme Court to prevent the protest, which they say "would cause severe loss", and demanded compensation for losses suffered during a similar rally planned over the weekend that was foiled by a security crackdown. The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power. A weeks-long sit-in by its supporters earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam paper leaks. The latest demonstrations erupted after The Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems.

Oct 16 : The Asian Tour postponed its season-ending Saudi International indefinitely on Friday in the aftermath of a deadly attack on the international airport in Riyadh, where the tournament was scheduled to take place next month. Yemen's Houthi movement has been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, including last weekend's attack on the capital that killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300. "The decision to postpone was taken following an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and ensuring the event is delivered to a standard befitting its international stature," an Asian Tour statement said. The $5 million flagship event, which is sponsored by the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), was scheduled to take place at Riyadh Golf Club from November 18 to 21. "The PIF Saudi International is one of the most important events on the Asian Tour calendar and we look forward to seeing our players compete in Riyadh in the future," Asian Tour Commissioner Cho Minn Thant said.

Source: Reuters

Oct 16 : The Asian Cup soccer tournament is on track to take place in Saudi Arabia early next year, local organisers said on Friday, but golf's Asian Tour has postponed the Saudi International indefinitely in the aftermath of a deadly attack on Riyadh. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed responsibility for Saturday's strike on Riyadh's international airport, which killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300. Australia also withdrew its team from the urban cycling World Championships on Friday, citing safety concerns over travelling to Riyadh, where the event is scheduled to take place in early November. The Six Kings Slam exhibition tennis tournament in Riyadh has already been moved from October to December, while FIFA on Thursday postponed the FIFAe Finals 2026 video game competition in the Saudi capital until an unspecified future date.

In that environment, serious questions were being asked over whether the 24-team Asian Cup could still go ahead in Saudi Arabia from January 7 to February 5 next year.  Asian soccer chief Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said earlier this week that a postponement of the continental championships until 2028 was possible if necessary, but the local organising committee said on Friday they were sticking to the original schedule. "Preparations across all organisational and operational areas are progressing according to the approved schedule, including work on venues, facilities and supporting services," it said in a statement. "(The LOC) will continue to monitor developments relevant to the tournament and ensure the appropriate conditions are in place for its successful delivery." ATTACKS DISRUPT SPORTS CALENDAR The $5 million Saudi International, which is sponsored by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), is the flagship event on the Asian Tour and had been scheduled to take place at Riyadh Golf Club from November 18-21. "The decision to postpone was taken following an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and ensuring the event is delivered to a standard befitting its international stature," an Asian Tour statement said. AusCycling said its decision to withdraw the Australian team from the urban World Championships was made "with the safety and wellbeing of our athletes and staff our highest priority". The Australian government is advising travellers to "reconsider" trips to Saudi Arabia in general and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport in particular "due to recent security incidents". The Saudi government has invested heavily in sport through the PIF in recent years and the Asian Cup was pitched as an early rehearsal for hosting the soccer World Cup in 2034. According to a report on US news website Semafor earlier this week, PIF is preparing to tell FIFA that it will be scaling back stadium plans for the 2034 tournament as part of a broader review of domestic spending. Reuters has contacted PIF for comment.

Source: Reuters
